account: Today I have followed my appointments: correspondence, a market walk, lunch, accounts, and tea at the east-bank cottage. I must now return for the 16:30 office appointment. The unusual feature is a recurring but unspecific rumor of a bridge or port change. I heard Townsfolk 03 and 23 discussing it; my secretary traced the inn's version to Townsfolk 03. The innkeeper denies proposing or announcing a change. The neighbour has also heard the rumor but has seen nothing unusual and has not yet identified a source. Builder reports the bridge passable with no confirmed defects. Freight reportedly found no damaged roads or ferry trouble and is offering deliveries, storage, and ferry rides. These offers might explain some talk about routes, but I have no evidence they represent a planned change or concealed purpose. Baker reports ample fresh bread and no special celebration; the neighbour describes quiet docks. No receipts, expense claims, or repair proposals reached the accounts meeting, and I authorized no repair spending. Builder is seeking specific maintenance needs and must supply written estimates before work. Secretary has helped investigate and confirmed the tea location. I also just heard freight speaking and shouting beyond intelligible range, so I cannot say what that was about. For now this looks like circulating hearsay amid ordinary trade, not a demonstrated scheme. I want the original source and concrete details before drawing conclusions.
